policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV spells the name Jehoaddin, transliterating the ketiv יהועדין with its final -in; the qere יְהוֹעַדָּן would give Jehoaddan.
ASV 'nor the children be put to death for the fathers' is passive, rendering the hophal qere יוּמָת; the ketiv qal ימות would read 'nor the children die'.

ASV 'the Valley of Salt' is a construct name whose English article cannot show whether the Hebrew carried the article (ketiv המלח) or not (qere מלח); the note on Sela is alternative_rendering and does not touch this unit.
ASV 'they fled every man to his tent' is singular, matching the ketiv לאהלו; the qere plural לְאֹהָלָיו would be rendered 'his tents'.

ASV 'Jehoash ... took Amaziah ... and came to Jerusalem, and brake down' keeps a single subject through the verb chain, rendering the singular qere וַיָּבֹא; the ketiv plural ויבאו would require 'and they came'.
